name: Phlox Tempest
iocPatterns: ISO file masquerading used in click fraud
usage of Choziosi and Chrome Loader tools
recommendedActions: Block known malicious 'ClickPirate' and 'Chrome Loader' infrastructure.
Implement strict policies regarding the installation of unverified browser extensions.
Alert users about the risks of downloading media files (e.g., .ISO) from unofficial social media links.
Monitor for scripts associated with Choziosi loader in web environment logs.
Block known malicious domains participating in malvertising campaigns.
Update web filters to flag and block recurring 'ClickPirate' payload delivery URLs.
Conduct internal audits of browser configurations on corporate workstations.
Implement EDR rules to detect common TTPs of the BitRAT and ShadowPad families.
campaignsText: Phlox Tempest's campaigns are characterized by high-volume, automated methods for clicking fraud and ad revenue. A significant portion of their activity revolves around the use of malvertising in social media spaces (like YouTube) to trick users into downloading ISO files to bypass detection systems. These campaigns frequently employ 'ClickPirate' and other related tools to drive fraudulent traffic. While they are a private sector actor, their technical reach is global, and they have been observed consistently utilizing both custom-built loaders (e.g., Choziosi) and broader malware families for information theft.
description: Phlox Tempest (DEV-0796) is a sophisticated, Israeli-based private sector threat actor primarily focused on high-volume financial gain through malvertising and click fraud operations. The group utilizes custom loaders and malicious Chrome extensions to compromise end-user devices for the purpose of monetizing web traffic and stealing sensitive information.
goals: The primary objectives of Phlox Tempest are financially motivated, specifically focusing on monetization through click fraud, unauthorized advertisement revenue generation, and the theft of sensitive user information. Their targeting profile is broad and non-discriminatory; however, they have demonstrated significant activity in high-value environments including the financial sector, aerospace, manufacturing, and government entities across various countries (including US, EU, and Asia).
